# Outline

Some kind of text outlining the project brief, maybe some stake holders like this:

- Alice
- Bob
- Carol

With [links](https://example.com) because obviously those should work.

Also, tabs, because you want to be able to organize your work well enough that you can use this VSTi as part of a template, where it's simply part of your master out and has everything already set up for you to "fill in the blanks".

# Instruments

Let's say you generally work with this kind of breakdown
## Beat

- instruments: ...
- filter chain: ...

## Lead

- instruments: ...
- filter chain: ...

## Melody

- instruments: ...
- filter chain: ...

## Vocals

- artist: ...
- filter chain: ...

And so on and so forth. And then let's have separate tabs for that, too.

# Beat

We could get real detailed about all aspects of the beat.

## Instruments

For example, which instruments are we using? maybe a couple of different ones for different sections, maybe there's notes on which thing it should be similar to, etc. etc

## Filter chain

And of course, is there a filter chain that we're already thinking of? If so, why not write that down as a flow chart?

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[EQ: profile 7]
  B[Sat: Saturn2]
  C[Dist: Decapitator]
  D[MTurboComp]
  E[Bassline]
  E2[Out]
  A --> B
  A --> |sidechain| E
  E --> E2
  B --> C
  B --> D
  C --> |50%| D
```
Super dumb, sure, but filter chains aren't

# Lead

A bit traditional, but... piano? organ? We could talk about which kind of spectral profile we're looking for, which specific VSTi, etc. etc.

In fact, let's just show what we want:

![image][1]

Images end up in the "images" tab as base64 encoded strings, so there's no loose images on disk to worry about. Once you remove the last reference to an image, it just gets deleted from the images list, so no stray images anywhere, either.

(And for obvious reasons, you can't edit the text in the images tab =P)

# Timeline

Charts are supported, too, so we can stub out a timeline gannt chart and then fill that in as the project progresses.


```mermaid
gantt
  title A Gantt Diagram
  dateFormat YYYY-MM-DD
  axisFormat %m/%d

  section Precomp
  Outline :done, o1, 2024-01-01, 10d
  Instrument selection :active, ins, after o1, 8d

  section Preapproval
  Soundbite :sb, 2024-01-20, 1d
  Teaser :ts, after sb, 2d

  section Full track
  Main :m, 2024-01-24, 7d
  Vocals :v, after m, 4d
  Candy :c, after v, 1d
```
Or, of course, you can just split it up into multiple charts. Why not? It's just markdown.
